description: A function whose only parameter is an object binding pattern declared no parameters at all, so no argument taint ever entered one -- and the options object is the shape most modern TypeScript is written in (measured on documenso: 3239 local call edges landed on a callee declaring no parameters). Four routes assert the taint now crosses: a plain binding, a defaulted binding, a nested and renamed binding, and a spread whose keys nobody wrote. Two assert it crosses into ONE binding rather than all of them: /count and /by-owner file the caller's value under a key no binding on the path to the interpreter reads, and reporting either would mean the fix had traded recall for noise.

expected.note: the caller's value arrives through a destructured parameter and reaches the statement
a defaulted binding is still a binding; the caller supplies the value and the default decides nothing
a nested binding read under another name still reads the property the call site filed
a spread leaves keys nobody wrote, so no binding can be ruled out and the whole argument is handed over
